articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Real Time Computing: The Future with MASCOT' (Digest No.101)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Real Time Computing: The Future with MASCOT
IEE Colloquium on Real Time Computing: The Future with MASCOT
abstract: The Data Orientated Requirements Implementation Scheme (DORIS) is a set of integrated methods for the development of real time, embedded, multi-processor systems. It covers the whole of the development life cycle from requirements elicitation and system definition, through design, and on into implementation in software and digital hardware. It has been specially formulated to promote the highest levels of integrity in digital and software system development. The unifying theme which runs through all aspects of DORIS is dataflow, and it draws on existing data flow methods where possible and appropriate. The principal component methods are: CORE, MASCOT, and DIA. The author outlines the principal architectural concepts and indicates some of the effects on Mascot design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mascot monitoring and control facilities in an Ada environment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Real Time Computing: The Future with MASCOT
abstract: This work is concerned with the development of Mascot style monitoring, control and error reporting facilities to support the use of the Mascot 3 design method using the Ada language as an implementation vehicle. The work has been carried out over a period of time and considered a range of mapping options between the Mascot run-time model and Ada. The selected method offered a number of advantages in terms of the constraints placed on the use of the language features and the amount of cooperation required from the program writer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Real Time Computing: The Future with MASCOT
abstract: Over the past few years there has been an increased awareness of the need for methods to cover the complete software development life-cycle. There are a large number of methods available. No one method covers the complete development process. The paper gives a brief sketch of five of the most widely mentioned methods: CORE, Yourdon, JSD, SSADM and MASCOT3. It then compares them from the points of view of techniques and representations, method and life-cycle coverage. Finally some possible combinations of methods which give good life-cycle coverage are suggested and related to the use of Ada as the preferred programming language.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Real Time Computing: The Future with MASCOT
abstract: The author looks at methods of structuring in Ada and compares them with the philosophy adopted in MASCOT. He shows that, with the current generation of computers, some of the design attitudes built into MASCOT remain a sensible and plausible way to design real time systems. He discusses hiding of asynchrony and encapsulation versus protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
